note: Ice hockey's built-in earlier seasons (docs/design/hockey.md, "Earlier seasons", "Computed seasons", "NHL 08 and NHL 09"). Five are an EA edition's ratings of an NHL season, joined to the NHL's own rosters of that season for positions and birth countries; two (NHL 08, NHL 09) convert an edition's attributes onto NHL 07's overalls (`converted`); the rest are computed from the players' season statistics (`computed`: the Hockey Databank for the seasons to 2009/10, MoneyPuck.com after). node scripts/sync-nhl-seasons.mjs writes scripts/data/nhl-seasons/<id>.json from the downloads pinned in scripts/data/nhl-seasons-sources.json; node scripts/build-nhl-seasons.mjs builds each season's clubs and nations; node scripts/build-club-maps.mjs --league=nhl builds each era's map from the clubs and `maps`. A season's clubs are `teams` where it lists the season (by the NHL's code then, `franchise` today's club, `id` the era's own id where the club has moved or been renamed since, `home` its arena's location [lon, lat]), else `eras`: every franchise's identities and arenas by season, the defunct Seals and Barons under nhl-cleveland-barons.

rescale.note: The three classic seasons' overalls (NHLPA '93, NHL '94, NHL 95) run far wider than today's, and the match model was tuned on NHL 27's: by the player's choice (2026-11-08) a season with `rescale` maps every overall onto this reference, rank for rank. An overall takes the reference rating at its mid-rank among the season's rated players (the mean of the first and last places it holds in their ascending order), so ties stay ties and nobody passes anybody. Goalies and skaters share one ordering, as they do in the reference. The snapshots and the audit keep the games' own overalls.
rescale.reference: NHL 27's built-in clubs as the game fields them: the 733 players of the 32 squads in src/data/clubs.hockey.js (rosters of 2026-11-07), EA's ratings and the marked estimates

computed.note: The seasons no EA edition rates in full (docs/design/hockey.md, "Computed seasons"), computed from the players' season statistics by the rule in scripts/lib/nhl-computed.mjs and read off NHL 27's squads group by group (`histograms`: the 433 forwards, 236 defenders and 64 goalies of the 32 built-in clubs, rosters of 2026-11-07, EA's ratings and the marked estimates; frozen here so a later rollover leaves these seasons as they are). `sources` names each statistics source, `calibration` the full editions the rule is measured against (scripts/data/nhl-seasons/calibration.json).

hdb.compiler: the Hockey Databank, version 13.0 of 10 July 2018 (maintained through the hockey-databank Yahoo group), as published at github.com/rippinrobr/hockey-databank
hdb.licence: free use of the data, a commercial product included, with the Hockey Databank's attribution statement displayed in its entirety (its readme)
hdb.attribution: The information used herein was obtained free of charge from and is copyrighted by the Hockey Databank project.  For more information about the Hockey Databank project please visit http://sports.groups.yahoo.com/group/hockey-databank
hdb.nation: the Hockey Databank's birth country (a birth it gives in the USSR, Czechoslovakia or Yugoslavia counts for the country the birth city is in today)

moneypuck.compiler: MoneyPuck.com's season summaries and game-by-game player data (moneypuck.com/data.htm)
moneypuck.licence: free to use for non-commercial purposes, crediting MoneyPuck.com (moneypuck.com/data.htm)
moneypuck.attribution: Statistics from MoneyPuck.com. Where its player lookup gives no nationality, the birth country is the Hockey Databank's: "The information used herein was obtained free of charge from and is copyrighted by the Hockey Databank project.  For more information about the Hockey Databank project please visit http://sports.groups.yahoo.com/group/hockey-databank"
moneypuck.nation: the nationality MoneyPuck.com's player lookup gives (the NHL's); where it gives none, the Hockey Databank's birth country of the one player of 2008/09 to 2017/18 with that name

converted.note: NHL 08 and NHL 09 publish their players' attributes but no overall (docs/design/hockey.md, "NHL 08 and NHL 09"): each player's score is the plain mean of his skill attributes, ranked within his group over the edition's club players and read off NHL 07's EA overalls in that group (`histograms`: the 515 forwards, 259 defenders and 84 goalies of scripts/data/nhl-seasons/nhl-2007.json). The seasons play on NHL 07's scale, as NHL 07 does.

seasons.label: NHLPA 93
seasons.compiler: the cartridge's attributes, exported with the NHL Hockey Roster Tool and posted by Von Ozbourne on forum.nhl94.com (topic 37373, September 2025)
seasons.overall: NHL '94's weights on the cartridge's displayed attributes (the game shows no overall): floor(sum of weight x floor(value x 20 / 3) / sum of weights)

seasons.label: NHL 94
seasons.compiler: KinGraph's sheet of the cartridge's attributes (NHL94 Players w Formula, forum.nhl94.com topic 19828)
seasons.overall: the game's own rule, reverse-engineered by wboy (forum.nhl94.com topic 228), from the cartridge's 0-6 attributes

seasons.label: NHL 95
seasons.compiler: Jon Morris's NHL 95 sheet (nhl-95.com), the Genesis game's overalls; the Rangers' skaters from Segathon's NHL 95 ratings

seasons.label: NHL 07
seasons.compiler: IGN's NHL 07 ratings pages (sports.ign.com/nhl07, EA's ratings), archived by the Wayback Machine
seasons.nation: EA's Country field in IGN's NHL 08 pages (sports.ign.com/nhl08, one year on) where it names the player, else the NHL's birth country

seasons.label: NHL 22
seasons.compiler: NHLRatings.net's team pages (a fan site that lists EA's ratings and names no source), as CommonCrawl captured them from January to May 2022: EA's launch rosters and ratings; EA's own launch lists add two players the pages leave out
seasons.overall: EA's NHL 22 launch ratings as the site lists them: every player EA's own launch lists rate (the top 50 and the top ten at each position) has EA's overall there
seasons.nation: EA's nationality where EA's launch lists name the player, else the NHL's birth country

seasons.label: NHL 08, converted
seasons.compiler: IGN's NHL 08 team pages (sports.ign.com/nhl08, EA's attributes, no overall), archived by the Wayback Machine
seasons.overall: converted: the mean of EA's skill attributes, ranked within each group and read off NHL 07's EA overalls in that group
seasons.nation: EA's Country field on IGN's NHL 08 pages, else the Hockey Databank's birth country

seasons.label: NHL 09, converted
seasons.compiler: IGN's NHL 09 team pages (sports.ign.com/nhl09, EA's attributes before the game's release; IGN: the overalls were not ready), archived by the Wayback Machine on 16-18 August 2008
seasons.overall: converted: the mean of EA's skill attributes, ranked within each group and read off NHL 07's EA overalls in that group
seasons.nation: EA's Country field on IGN's NHL 08 pages (one year before) where it names the player, else the Hockey Databank's birth country

eras.note: Every franchise's identity and arena by season (a season named by the year it ends), for the seasons `teams` does not list: `id` is the era's own id where the club has moved or been renamed since, `home` the arena's location [lon, lat]. From 1980/81 the arenas, cities and points are those of the earlier research (Wikipedia's arena and franchise articles, read 2026-11-07), the points the NHL's own where `teams` gives them; before 1980/81 from Wikipedia's arena articles; every article used is pinned to its revision in `wikipedia`. Codes are the NHL's, as Wikipedia's list of NHL team abbreviations gives them. A season whose club played in two arenas plays in the one that hosted most of its home games (Wikipedia's season articles): the 1967/68 Kings at the Forum (21 of 37), the 1967/68 Rangers at the third Madison Square Garden (26 of 37), the 1979/80 Red Wings at Joe Louis Arena (28 of 40), the 1979/80 Whalers at the Springfield Civic Center (22 of 40), the 1995/96 Senators at the Palladium (26 of 41), the 1997/98 Capitals at the MCI Center (31 of 41), the 1998/99 Maple Leafs at Maple Leaf Gardens (27 of 41), the 2003/04 Coyotes at Glendale Arena (28 of 41), the 2018/19 and 2019/20 Islanders at Nassau Coliseum (21 of 41, 24 of 35). nhl-cleveland-barons is the defunct franchise of the Oakland Seals, California Golden Seals and Cleveland Barons, merged into the Minnesota North Stars in 1978.
